newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Jailed Ivorian journalists denied bail.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Ivorian journalists denied bail.

text.p: A court in Ivory Coast turned down a bail application on Monday from three opposition journalists serving two-year jail terms for insulting President Henri Konan Bedie, their lawyer said.

The three -- Abou Drahamane Sangare, Freedom Neruda and Emmanuel Kore of the opposition newspaper La Voie -- rejected conditions for a presidential pardon in August, dismissing them as political blackmail. They are pressing ahead with an appeal to the supreme court and applied for bail pending the outcome.
Lawyer Jacques-Andre Monoko Daligou told Reuters all three appeared in court on Monday. The judge turned down the bail application but gave no reason, he said.

Bedie signed a decree in August offering pardons to mark 36 years of national independence. "My clients have rejected the condition set by the authorities. They look on it as political blackmail," Daligou said at the time.

La Voie, published by the Ivorian Popular Front (FPI), ran an article in December suggesting Bedie's presence had brought local soccer team ASEC bad luck when Orlando Pirates of South Africa defeated them in the final of the African Champions Cup.

Kore and publications director Sangare, who is also FPI deputy leader, were jailed by a magistrate's court on December 28. The court fined the newspaper three million CFA francs ($6,000). It jailed Neruda for two years on January 11.
The United States embassy in Abidjan and international press organisations denounced the sentences as excessive.
